title: Rat subthalamic stimulation: Evaluating stimulation-induced dyskinesias, choosing stimulation currents and evaluating the anti-akinetic effect in the cylinder test
author: Huotarinen, Leino, et al.
materials: Striata were harvested at −15 °C in a cryotome (CM3050 S, Leica, Wetzlar, Germany) with a 3 mm sampling punch; they were then stored at −80 °C. For western blotting (WB), the striata were homogenized and boiled for 10 min in 1% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) and then sonicated. Their protein content was measured using DC protein assays (Biorad, Hercules, CA, USA) with a UV-2401PC spectrophotometer (Shimadzu, Kyoto, Japan) and a UV Probe 2.31 program (Shimadzu, Kyoto, Japan). Equal amounts of protein (20 μg) was then loaded onto 10% SDS gels (Biorad TGX), which were blotted with Biorad Turboblotter on PVDF membranes. Tyrosine hydroxylase was probed with an anti-tyorsine hydroxylase (TH) antibody (1:4000; #2792, Cell Signaling Technology, Danvers, MA, USA), visualized with Pierce ECL+ (ThermoFisher, Waltham, MA, USA),and detected with Typhoon 9000 chemifluorescence (GE Healthcare, Chicago, IL, USA). Loading control was performed by re-probing the same membrane with anti-actin (1:30000, Merck Millipore #MAB1501, Billerica, MA, USA). The signal intensity was quantified using ImageJ 1.49 (Mac version, NIH image, [25]), and the lesioned side was compared to the un-lesioned side.

steps.title: Harvest and store striata tissue
steps.instruction: Using a cryotome (CM3050 S, Leica) set to –15 °C, punch out the striata with a 3 mm sampling punch, then immediately store the tissue at –80 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Homogenize and solubilize proteins
steps.instruction: Homogenize the frozen striata, boil the homogenate for 10 min in 1 % SDS, and subsequently sonicate the sample to ensure complete solubilization.

steps.title: Determine protein concentration
steps.instruction: Measure protein content with a DC protein assay (Bio‑Rad) using a UV‑2401PC spectrophotometer (Shimadzu) operated with the UV Probe 2.31 program.

steps.title: Prepare SDS‑PAGE and transfer
steps.instruction: Load equal amounts of protein (20 µg) onto 10 % SDS‑PAGE gels (Bio‑Rad TGX), run the gel, and transfer proteins onto PVDF membranes using a Bio‑Rad Turboblotter.

steps.title: Probe for tyrosine hydroxylase
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with anti‑tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) antibody (1:4000; #2792, Cell Signaling Technology), visualize with Pierce ECL+ (ThermoFisher), and detect chemifluorescence using a Typhoon 9000 (GE Healthcare).

steps.title: Perform loading control
steps.instruction: Re‑probe the same membrane with anti‑actin antibody (1:30 000; #MAB1501, Merck Millipore) to serve as a loading control.

steps.title: Quantify band intensities
steps.instruction: Analyze the chemifluorescence images with ImageJ 1.49 (Mac version) and compare signal intensities between the lesioned and un‑lesioned sides.

steps.title: Section STN for cresyl violet staining
steps.instruction: Cut coronal sections of 40 µm thickness from the subthalamic nucleus (STN) region using the cryotome.

steps.title: Stain sections with cresyl violet
steps.instruction: Stain the 40 µm sections in 0.2 % cresyl violet solution.

steps.title: Microscopic analysis of stained sections
steps.instruction: Examine the stained sections under a light microscope and compare the anatomy to the Paxinos and Watson rat brain atlas.
